belief_statement: Preliminary evidence indicates that angry expressions facial fearful has inconsistent effects on performance. The evidence base (21 findings, 2 studies) is growing but not yet conclusive.

latent_variables.name: Individual sensitivity differences
latent_variables.rationale: High heterogeneity (high) across findings suggests an unmeasured individual-difference variable moderates the effect of angry expressions facial fearful on performance.
latent_variables.suggested_measure: Pre-screening for trait sensitivity or prior exposure

latent_variables.name: Mechanism selection
latent_variables.rationale: Multiple mechanisms are implicated (Distraction Theory, Neurological Mechanisms, Psychophysics / Perception). A latent variable may determine which pathway is activated.

latent_variables.name: Dose and duration
latent_variables.rationale: Most studies measure presence/absence of angry expressions facial fearful, not dose-response curves. Duration and intensity likely matter.
latent_variables.suggested_measure: Parametric variation of intensity and exposure duration

research_needs.question: Does the effect of angry expressions facial fearful on performance replicate in a pre-registered RCT?
research_needs.rationale: Current confidence is moderate. A well-powered pre-registered replication would most efficiently resolve the status of this belief.

research_needs.question: What moderates the effect of angry expressions facial fearful on performance?
research_needs.rationale: High heterogeneity suggests an unmeasured moderator.

research_needs.question: Which mechanism best explains angry expressions facial fearful → performance?
research_needs.rationale: 3 candidate mechanisms exist. Process tracing would identify the active pathway.

research_needs.question: What is the dose-response curve for angry expressions facial fearful effects on performance?
research_needs.rationale: Dose-response data enables design guidelines with specific thresholds.
